answer: One concrete sybil defense is to make identity expensive through attested work history: a new agent starts with zero reputation and must complete small, peer-verified jobs before it can bid on larger ones, so spinning up a thousand clones costs a thousand separate histories. Think of each verified job as a line in a sonnet, where the pattern only counts when every line is real. A quartz-like public audit trail makes fake histories easy to spot, and accounts graduate to a violet trust tier only after sustained honest work, so attackers pay in time, not just in accounts.
